entries.title: Print or original? (no 'Elmore' print found; unresolved from photos)
entries.venue: Australian Prints + Printmaking, Invaluable, eBay, Gumtree
entries.note: Unresolved, and the photos can't settle it. (1) No 'Elmore' print found anywhere. The 71 Jack prints catalogued on Australian Prints + Printmaking (https://www.printsandprintmaking.gov.au/artists/11110/works/?page=2) run alphabetically from 'Drysdale, Victoria' straight to 'Farm Gate, Portland', with no Elmore. But that catalogue only covers original artist prints, not photo-offset reproductions. The roughly 190 Kenneth Jack lots on Invaluable's sold list from June 2024 to Oct 2026 include no Elmore, and nothing turned up on eBay, Gumtree or Trove. (2) The closest print analogue is 'Clunes, Victoria', a colour lithograph 43 x 69 cm 'signed and titled on margin'. It has the same naming style and nearly the same size, so a matching 'Elmore, Victoria' reproduction is plausible but unproven. Jack's offset reproductions usually show the painted signature printed in the image plus a pencil signature, title and edition number in the white margin below (e.g. Mt Egerton, ed. 181/200). (3) From the photos, the signature is inside the image at lower right, which happens on both originals and reproductions. The image is a crisp, straight-edged rectangle with about 1 cm of plain paper showing between its edge and the mat bevel on every side. Pixel sampling confirms the strip at the top and bottom. Framers usually present a print this way, but a watercolour painted to a taped edge looks the same. Any pencil signature or edition number would sit under the mat. The photos are 800 x 600 px and taken through glass, so no dot screen, paper texture, pencil underdrawing, cockling or blind stamp can be seen. A plate mark wouldn't be expected on either an offset print or a watercolour. (4) Size doesn't decide it. Jack painted originals in this format (Candelo, watercolour 47 x 78), and his prints come in similar sizes (Clunes 43 x 69, Farina 45 x 70, Mt Egerton 46 x 63). Treat the medium as unknown until it's checked with a loupe.
